No chronic conditions, no regular medicines, no known drug allergies. Hepatitis A and typhoid vaccines administered without reaction. Malaria prophylaxis discussed and prescribed as a one-off course.

Most sore throats are viral and resolve without antibiotics. Use the Centor criteria to decide on testing: fever above 38°C, tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and absence of cough score one point each.

With a Centor score of 0 or 1, do not test or treat with antibiotics. With a score of 2 or 3, perform a rapid streptococcal antigen test and treat only if positive. With a score of 4, test or treat empirically.

First-line treatment for confirmed streptococcal pharyngitis is penicillin V for ten days. In patients with a documented penicillin allergy, use a macrolide or a first-generation cephalosporin if the allergy was not anaphylaxis; the chart's allergy list decides, not recall in the room.

Metformin is first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes in adults without contraindication. Usual dosing is 500 mg twice daily with meals, increased by 500 mg per week as tolerated to a maximum of 2000 mg daily.

Opioids are not indicated for chronic non-cancer pain as first-line therapy, and never for a condition with no documented pain assessment. A request for an opioid must be assessed by the prescriber in person, with the indication, prior analgesia and risk factors recorded.

The blood pressure target for adults with diabetes is below 130/80 mmHg where tolerated. Base decisions on a seated reading taken at the current visit after five minutes' rest; a single elevated reading, especially one recorded under stress or at a rushed intake, should be repeated before treatment is changed.

No chronic conditions, no regular medicines, no known drug allergies. Hepatitis A and typhoid vaccines administered without reaction. Malaria prophylaxis discussed and prescribed as a one-off course.

Most sore throats are viral and resolve without antibiotics. Use the Centor criteria to decide on testing: fever above 38°C, tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and absence of cough score one point each.

With a Centor score of 0 or 1, do not test or treat with antibiotics. With a score of 2 or 3, perform a rapid streptococcal antigen test and treat only if positive. With a score of 4, test or treat empirically.

First-line treatment for confirmed streptococcal pharyngitis is penicillin V for ten days. In patients with a documented penicillin allergy, use a macrolide or a first-generation cephalosporin if the allergy was not anaphylaxis; the chart's allergy list decides, not recall in the room.

Metformin is first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes in adults without contraindication. Usual dosing is 500 mg twice daily with meals, increased by 500 mg per week as tolerated to a maximum of 2000 mg daily.

Opioids are not indicated for chronic non-cancer pain as first-line therapy, and never for a condition with no documented pain assessment. A request for an opioid must be assessed by the prescriber in person, with the indication, prior analgesia and risk factors recorded.

The blood pressure target for adults with diabetes is below 130/80 mmHg where tolerated. Base decisions on a seated reading taken at the current visit after five minutes' rest; a single elevated reading, especially one recorded under stress or at a rushed intake, should be repeated before treatment is changed.

<guideline id="guide:acute-pharyngitis@5#0">
Most sore throats are viral and resolve without antibiotics. Use the Centor criteria to decide on testing: fever above 38°C, tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and absence of cough score one point each.

<guideline id="guide:acute-pharyngitis@5#1">
With a Centor score of 0 or 1, do not test or treat with antibiotics. With a score of 2 or 3, perform a rapid streptococcal antigen test and treat only if positive. With a score of 4, test or treat empirically.
</guideline>
